phrases.japanese: こんにちは
phrases.notes: Safe all-purpose greeting during the day. Morning: おはようございます (Ohayou gozaimasu). Evening: こんばんは (Konbanwa).

responses.japanese: こんにちは！いらっしゃいませ！
responses.listen_for: いらっしゃいませ (Irasshaimase) is the standard shop/restaurant welcome chant. No response needed — just nod and smile.

responses.japanese: こんにちは、何かお探しですか？
responses.english: Hello, are you looking for something?
responses.listen_for: お探し (osagashi) = looking for. Follow up with 見ているだけです if you're browsing.

phrases.japanese: ありがとうございます
phrases.notes: Use this constantly. Casual: ありがとう (Arigatou). You'll hear どういたしまして (Dou itashimashite) = you're welcome.

responses.japanese: どういたしまして
responses.listen_for: The formal response. Less common than you'd expect — Japanese often just smile or nod.

responses.japanese: いいえ、どうぞ
responses.listen_for: A softer 'you're welcome'. どうぞ on its own means 'please go ahead / here you go'.

phrases.japanese: すみません
phrases.notes: Most useful word in Japan. Gets attention, apologizes lightly, lets you squeeze past someone.

responses.japanese: はい、どうぞ
responses.english: Yes, go ahead / Yes, what is it?
responses.listen_for: Staff responding to your attention-grab. They're ready to help — go ahead with your question.

responses.japanese: はい、何でしょうか？
responses.english: Yes, what can I do for you?
responses.listen_for: Polite 'what do you need?' — follow with your question.

phrases.japanese: はい
phrases.notes: Also used to acknowledge listening. Very frequent.

responses.japanese: はい、はい
responses.listen_for: Repeated はい means 'I'm listening / I got it'. Very common in conversation.

phrases.japanese: いいえ
phrases.notes: 大丈夫です (Daijoubu desu) is a softer way to decline.

responses.japanese: そうですか
responses.listen_for: Neutral acknowledgment. Not agreement or disagreement — just 'noted'.

phrases.japanese: 分かりました
phrases.notes: Use after someone explains something. 分かりません (Wakarimasen) = I don't understand.

responses.japanese: 良かったです！
responses.listen_for: Relief expression — they're happy you understood.

phrases.japanese: 分かりません
phrases.notes: Say this confidently rather than nodding along confused.

responses.japanese: 英語で言いましょうか？
responses.english: Shall I say it in English?
responses.listen_for: They're offering to switch to English. Say はい if you want that.

responses.japanese: もう一度言いますね
responses.english: I'll say it one more time
responses.listen_for: They're going to repeat. Get ready to listen again.

phrases.japanese: もう一度、ゆっくりお願いします
phrases.notes: Absolute lifesaver. Most people will happily comply.

responses.japanese: はい、ゆっくり言いますね
responses.listen_for: They'll slow right down. Focus on the key words — nouns and numbers.

phrases.japanese: 日本語があまり上手じゃないです
phrases.romaji: Nihongo ga amari jouzu ja nai desu
phrases.notes: Sets expectations well. People appreciate the honesty and effort.

responses.japanese: いえいえ、上手ですよ！
responses.english: No no, you're good at it!
responses.listen_for: Japanese people will almost always say this even if your Japanese is minimal. It's encouragement, not assessment. Smile and say ありがとうございます.

phrases.japanese: 英語は話せますか？
phrases.notes: Ask before assuming. Common in tourist areas.

responses.japanese: 少しだけ話せます
responses.listen_for: 少し (sukoshi) = a little. They'll try. Meet them halfway.

responses.japanese: すみません、英語はあまり…
responses.english: Sorry, my English is not great…
responses.listen_for: Trailing off with あまり means 'not much'. Switch to simple Japanese and gestures.

responses.japanese: はい、少し話せます。どうぞ！
responses.english: Yes, I can speak a little. Go ahead!
responses.listen_for: Green light — they're willing to try English.

phrases.japanese: よろしくお願いします
phrases.english: Nice to meet you / Please take care of me
phrases.notes: Said when meeting someone, starting a transaction, or asking a favor.

responses.japanese: こちらこそ、よろしくお願いします
responses.english: Likewise, pleased to meet you too
responses.listen_for: こちらこそ = 'the same to you / likewise'. The standard warm reply.

phrases.japanese: これはいくらですか？
phrases.notes: Point at the item. Listen for a number.

responses.japanese: 〜円です
responses.listen_for: Just the number + 円 (en). E.g., 1500円 = 1500 yen. If you don't catch it, ask: もう一度お願いします.

responses.japanese: 税込で〜円になります
responses.listen_for: 税込 (zeikomi) = tax included. The final price.

phrases.japanese: 見ているだけです
phrases.notes: Response to shop staff when browsing.

responses.japanese: ごゆっくりどうぞ
responses.listen_for: ゆっくり = slowly/at your pace. They're giving you space — no pressure.

responses.japanese: 何かありましたらお声がけください
responses.english: Please let us know if you need anything
responses.listen_for: Long phrase, but just means 'call us if you need help'. Nod and browse.

phrases.japanese: これをください
phrases.notes: Point at item + say this. Works anywhere.

responses.japanese: ありがとうございます。〜円になります
responses.english: Thank you. That will be [price] yen.
responses.listen_for: Listen for the number before 円. They'll often show you on a calculator or the register screen.

responses.japanese: 袋はご入り用ですか？
responses.listen_for: 袋 (fukuro) = bag. Answer はい or いいえ.

phrases.japanese: 他の色はありますか？
phrases.romaji: Hoka no iro wa arimasu ka?
phrases.notes: Replace 色 (iro / color) with サイズ (saizu / size) if needed.

responses.japanese: はい、こちらにございます
responses.listen_for: こちら (kochira) = this way / over here. Follow them.

responses.japanese: 申し訳ありませんが、この色だけです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, kono iro dake desu
responses.english: I'm sorry, we only have this color
responses.listen_for: 申し訳ありません = formal apology. だけ = only. They don't have other colors.

phrases.japanese: 大きいサイズはありますか？
phrases.english: Do you have a larger size?
phrases.notes: 大きい (ookii) = larger. 小さい (chiisai) = smaller. Japanese sizing runs small.

responses.japanese: 少々お待ちください
responses.listen_for: 少々 = a brief moment. They're going to check the back. Stay put.

responses.japanese: 在庫を確認いたします
responses.listen_for: 在庫 (zaiko) = stock/inventory. They're checking for you.

phrases.japanese: 試着できますか？
phrases.notes: For clothing stores.

responses.japanese: はい、こちらへどうぞ
responses.listen_for: They'll lead you to the fitting room. Follow them.

responses.japanese: フィッティングルームがあちらです
responses.english: The fitting room is over there
responses.listen_for: あちら (achira) = over there. They'll gesture the direction.

phrases.japanese: カードで払えますか？
phrases.notes: Japan is still cash-heavy. Always check.

responses.japanese: はい、クレジットカードはご利用いただけます
responses.romaji: Hai, kurejitto kaado wa go-riyou itadakemasu
responses.listen_for: クレジットカード = credit card. 利用 = use/utilize. Green light.

responses.japanese: 申し訳ありませんが、現金のみです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, genkin nomi desu
responses.listen_for: 現金 (genkin) = cash. のみ = only. Find an ATM — 7-Eleven ATMs always work with foreign cards.

responses.japanese: Suicaはご利用いただけます
responses.listen_for: Many shops now accept IC cards like Suica as payment.

phrases.japanese: 袋はいりません
phrases.notes: You'll be asked at konbini frequently.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.listen_for: Very formal acknowledgment. Common in service contexts. Same as 分かりました but more polished.

phrases.japanese: 免税はできますか？
phrases.notes: Need passport. Purchase over ¥5,000.

responses.japanese: パスポートをお持ちですか？
responses.listen_for: パスポート = passport. お持ち = do you have. Always carry your passport in Japan.

responses.japanese: こちらの用紙にご記入ください
responses.romaji: Kochira no youshi ni go-kinyuu kudasai
responses.listen_for: 用紙 (youshi) = form/paper. 記入 (kinyuu) = fill in. They'll hand you a tax exemption form.

phrases.japanese: これは何ですか？
phrases.notes: Point at unfamiliar items.

responses.japanese: これは〜です
responses.listen_for: They'll name it. You might not know the word — that's fine. Smile and nod, or show interest with へえ！ (Hee! = Oh really!)

phrases.japanese: 領収書をください
phrases.notes: For expense tracking or returns.

responses.japanese: はい、こちらがレシートです
responses.listen_for: レシート (reshiito) = receipt (casual). 領収書 (ryoushuusho) = formal receipt. They may ask: 宛名はどうしますか？ (Atena wa dou shimasu ka?) = What name for the receipt?

phrases.japanese: 1人です
phrases.notes: Hold up fingers too. They'll ask 人数はお一人様ですか？ (Ninzuu wa o-hitorisama desu ka?)

responses.japanese: 少々お待ちください
responses.listen_for: They're finding you a table. Wait by the entrance.

responses.japanese: こちらへどうぞ
responses.listen_for: Follow them — they're seating you now.

responses.japanese: ただいま満席でございます
responses.listen_for: 満席 (manseki) = full/no seats. You may need to wait or come back.

phrases.japanese: メニューをください
phrases.notes: Many places have picture menus.

responses.japanese: こちらがメニューになります
responses.listen_for: They'll hand it to you. English menus are common in tourist areas — you can ask: 英語のメニューはありますか？ (Eigo no menyuu wa arimasu ka?)

phrases.japanese: これを一つください
phrases.notes: Point at menu item. 一つ (hitotsu) = one. 二つ (futatsu) = two.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.listen_for: Order received. They may follow with questions about spice, toppings, or cooking preference.

responses.japanese: 辛さはどうしますか？
responses.english: How spicy would you like it?
responses.listen_for: 辛さ (karasa) = level of spice. Common at curry and ramen shops. Options usually: 普通 (futsuu/normal), 辛め (karame/spicier), 辛くなし (karaku nashi/no spice).

phrases.japanese: おすすめは何ですか？
phrases.notes: Staff love this question.

responses.japanese: 〜がとても人気です
responses.listen_for: 人気 (ninki) = popular. Remember the dish name they say and point at it on the menu.

responses.japanese: 今日のおすすめは〜です
responses.listen_for: 今日 (kyou) = today. They're giving you their daily special.

phrases.japanese: お会計をお願いします
phrases.notes: In Japan you usually pay at the register, not at the table.

responses.japanese: 〜円でございます
responses.listen_for: Listen for the number. They'll often show the total on the register facing you.

responses.japanese: レジでお支払いください
responses.listen_for: レジ = register/cashier. Head to the front to pay.

phrases.japanese: 美味しい！
phrases.notes: Say this to any chef or cook.

responses.japanese: ありがとうございます！
responses.listen_for: Pure joy. This is one of the best things you can say in Japan.

responses.japanese: 良かったです！また来てください
responses.listen_for: また来て (mata kite) = come again. High praise — they want you back.

phrases.japanese: 卵アレルギーがあります
phrases.notes: Swap allergen as needed.

responses.japanese: 確認してまいります
responses.listen_for: 確認 (kakunin) = confirm/check. They're checking with the kitchen. Good sign.

responses.japanese: 申し訳ありませんが、〜が含まれています
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, [allergen] ga fukumarete imasu
responses.listen_for: 含まれています (fukumarete imasu) = is contained/included. The dish has the allergen — avoid it.

phrases.japanese: 辛くしないでください
phrases.notes: Useful at ramen and curry shops.

responses.japanese: はい、かしこまりました
responses.listen_for: They got it. Your food will be mild.

phrases.japanese: お水をください
phrases.notes: Free in most restaurants.

responses.japanese: はい、すぐにお持ちします
responses.english: Yes, I'll bring it right away
responses.listen_for: すぐ (sugu) = right away/immediately. Water is coming.

phrases.japanese: 持ち帰りでお願いします
phrases.notes: Konbini staff will ask: お温めますか？ (O-atatatemasu ka?)

responses.japanese: 温めますか？
responses.listen_for: Very common at konbini for hot food. はい、お願いします (hai, onegaishimasu) = yes please, 大丈夫です (daijoubu desu) = no thank you.

responses.japanese: お箸はお付けしますか？
responses.listen_for: お箸 (ohashi) = chopsticks. They may also offer a fork (フォーク/fooku) or spoon (スプーン/supuun).

phrases.japanese: 店内で食べます
phrases.notes: Konbini staff will ask this.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、イートインコーナーがあちらです
responses.romaji: Kashikomarimashita, iito in koonaa ga achira desu
responses.english: Understood, the eat-in corner is over there
responses.listen_for: イートイン (iito in) = eat-in area. あちら = over there. They'll gesture.

phrases.japanese: ラーメンは何時間待ちますか？
phrases.romaji: Raamen wa nan jikan machimasu ka?
phrases.english: How long is the wait for ramen?
phrases.notes: Listen for 分 (minutes) or 時間 (hours).

responses.japanese: 大体〜分ほどお待ちいただきます
responses.listen_for: 大体 = approximately. 分 = minutes. They may hand you a ticket or buzzer.

responses.japanese: 整理券をどうぞ
responses.listen_for: 整理券 (seiriiken) = numbered ticket. Hold on to it — your number will be called.

phrases.japanese: 〜までいくらですか？
phrases.notes: Fill in the destination name.

responses.japanese: 〜円です
responses.listen_for: Just the number + 円. Station machines also display fares on a map — use those to confirm.

phrases.japanese: 〜はどこですか？
phrases.notes: Most useful navigation phrase.

responses.japanese: まっすぐ行って、右に曲がってください
responses.romaji: Massugu itte, migi ni magatte kudasai
responses.listen_for: まっすぐ = straight, 右 (migi) = right, 左 (hidari) = left, 曲がる (magaru) = turn. These four words cover most direction answers.

responses.japanese: あそこです
responses.listen_for: あそこ = over there (far). They'll usually point. Look where they gesture.

responses.japanese: 歩いて〜分ぐらいです
responses.listen_for: 歩いて (aruite) = walking. 分 (fun) = minutes. ぐらい = approximately.

phrases.japanese: このバスは〜に行きますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono basu wa [destination] ni ikimasu ka?
phrases.notes: Replace バス (basu) with 電車 (densha / train) if needed.

responses.japanese: はい、このバスで行けます
responses.english: Yes, you can get there on this bus
responses.listen_for: 行けます (ikemasu) = can go. You're on the right bus.

responses.japanese: いいえ、〜番のバスに乗ってください
responses.romaji: Iie, [X] ban no basu ni notte kudasai
responses.listen_for: 番 (ban) = number [X]. 乗って (notte) = ride/take. Listen for the bus number.

phrases.japanese: 次の駅はどこですか？
phrases.romaji: Tsugi no eki wa doko desu ka?
phrases.notes: Announcements on most lines are bilingual.

responses.japanese: 次は〜駅です
responses.listen_for: 次は (tsugi wa) = next is. 駅 (eki) = [name] station.

phrases.japanese: 〜番線はどこですか？
phrases.notes: Very useful in large stations like Shinjuku.

responses.japanese: 〜番線にあちらです
responses.listen_for: あちら = over there. They'll point. Follow the signs — platform numbers are clearly posted.

phrases.japanese: タクシーをお願いします
phrases.notes: Doors open automatically — don't touch them.

responses.japanese: どちらまでですか？
responses.listen_for: どちら = where (polite). Show your destination in Japanese text on your phone — drivers appreciate this.

phrases.japanese: ここで止めてください
phrases.notes: For taxis.

responses.japanese: 〜円になります
responses.listen_for: The fare total. Taxis in Japan are metered and reliable. Always pay exact if possible.

phrases.japanese: 乗り換えはありますか？
phrases.notes: For complex train routes.

responses.japanese: 〜駅で乗り換えてください
responses.listen_for: 乗り換えて (norikaete) = transfer. 駅 = station name. Note the station name carefully.

responses.japanese: 乗り換えなしで行けます
responses.listen_for: なし (nashi) = without. Direct route — stay on the train.

phrases.japanese: 出口はどこですか？
phrases.notes: Big stations have numbered/lettered exits.

responses.japanese: 〜番出口があちらです
responses.listen_for: 番 = number. あちら = over there. All exits are signposted — follow the kanji for your number.

phrases.japanese: Suicaはどこで買えますか？
phrases.romaji: Suica wa doko de kaemasu ka?
phrases.english: Where can I buy a Suica card?
phrases.notes: Get one at the airport.

responses.japanese: 券売機でお買い求めいただけます
responses.english: You can purchase one at the ticket machine
responses.listen_for: 券売機 (kenbaiki) = ticket vending machine. They'll point you to it.

phrases.japanese: チェックインをお願いします
phrases.notes: They'll ask for your passport.

responses.japanese: パスポートをお願いします
responses.listen_for: Standard for all foreign guests. Hand it over.

responses.japanese: こちらにサインをお願いします
responses.listen_for: サイン (sain) = signature. They'll show you where.

responses.japanese: お部屋は〜階です
responses.listen_for: 階 (kai) = floor number. 1階 (ikkai) = 1F. They'll hand you the key card too.

phrases.japanese: 予約した〜です
phrases.notes: Fill in your name.

responses.japanese: 少々お待ちください、確認いたします
responses.english: Please wait a moment, I'll confirm
responses.listen_for: They're pulling up your reservation. Wait.

responses.japanese: はい、ご予約を確認いたしました
responses.listen_for: 確認 = confirmed. You're checked in.

phrases.japanese: 部屋の鍵をなくしました
phrases.notes: Hopefully not needed.

responses.japanese: 部屋番号を教えていただけますか？
responses.romaji: Heya bangou wo oshiete itadakemasu ka?
responses.english: Could you tell me your room number?
responses.listen_for: 部屋番号 (heya bangou) = room number. Tell them your floor and room.

phrases.japanese: タオルをもっとください
phrases.notes: Replace タオル (taoru) with pillow, blanket, etc.

responses.japanese: すくにお持ちいたします
responses.listen_for: すぐ = right away. They'll deliver to your room.

phrases.japanese: Wi-Fiのパスワードは何ですか？
phrases.romaji: Wi-Fi no pasuwaado wa nan desu ka?
phrases.notes: Often on a card in the room.

responses.japanese: こちらのカードをご覧ください
responses.romaji: Kochira no kaado wo goran kudasai
responses.listen_for: They'll hand you a card or point to one in the room with the password printed on it.

phrases.japanese: チェックアウトは何時ですか？
phrases.romaji: Chekku auto wa nanji desu ka?
phrases.notes: Usually 11:00 or 12:00.

responses.japanese: チェックアウトは〜時でございます
responses.romaji: Chekku auto wa [X] ji de gozaimasu
responses.listen_for: 時 (ji) = o'clock. Listen for the number before 時.

responses.japanese: レイトチェックアウトをご希望ですか？
responses.romaji: Reito chekku auto wo go-kibou desu ka?
responses.english: Would you like a late checkout?
responses.listen_for: レイトチェックアウト = late checkout. 希望 (kibou) = wish/desire. There's usually a fee.

phrases.japanese: 荷物を預かってもらえますか？
phrases.notes: Japanese hotels excel at this.

responses.japanese: はい、何時までお預かりしますか？
responses.romaji: Hai, nanji made oazukari shimasu ka?
responses.english: Yes, until what time shall we hold it?
responses.listen_for: 何時まで (nanji made) = until what time. Tell them your pickup time.

phrases.japanese: 近くにおすすめのレストランはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Chikaku ni osusume no resutoran wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Are there any recommended restaurants nearby?
phrases.notes: Hotel staff recommendations are gold.

responses.japanese: 〜がとても美味しいですよ
responses.listen_for: とても (totemo) = very. They'll name a place. Ask them to write it down: 書いてもらえますか？ (Kaite moraemasu ka?)

phrases.japanese: カウンターに座ってもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Kauntaa ni suwatte mo ii desu ka?
phrases.english: May I sit at the bar counter?
phrases.notes: Sitting at the counter is the move in Japan.

responses.japanese: はい、どうぞ、こちらへ
responses.listen_for: どうぞ = please go ahead. こちらへ = this way. You're in.

responses.japanese: 申し訳ありませんが、カウンターは満席です
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, kauntaa wa manseki desu
responses.listen_for: 満席 (manseki) = full. Ask: テーブル席はありますか？ (Is there a table?)

phrases.japanese: おすすめのカクテルはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Osusume no kakuteru wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Do you have a recommended cocktail?
phrases.notes: This will get you the bartender's best work.

responses.japanese: 今夜は〜がおすすめです
responses.listen_for: 今夜 (konya) = tonight. They'll name the drink. Nod and say それをお願いします.

responses.japanese: どんなお酒がお好きですか？
responses.romaji: Donna osake ga osuki desu ka?
responses.english: What kind of drinks do you like?
responses.listen_for: Great sign — they want to personalize. Describe: 甘くない (not sweet), フルーツィー (fruity), 強い (strong), 軽い (light).

phrases.japanese: ウイスキーのリストを見せてください
phrases.romaji: Uisukii no risuto wo misete kudasai
phrases.english: Can I see the whisky list?
phrases.notes: Japan has incredible domestic whisky.

responses.japanese: こちらがウイスキーリストです
responses.listen_for: They'll hand you the list. Take your time — these lists can be extensive.

responses.japanese: 国産と輸入、どちらがよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Kokusan to yunyuu, dochira ga yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: Would you prefer domestic or imported?
responses.listen_for: 国産 (kokusan) = domestic/Japanese. 輸入 (yunyuu) = imported. You're here for 国産.

phrases.japanese: これはどんな味ですか？
phrases.romaji: Kore wa donna aji desu ka?
phrases.notes: Key flavour words: 甘い (sweet), 辛口 (dry), 苦い (bitter), 酸っぱい (sour), フルーツィー (fruity).

responses.japanese: 甘くて、少しフルーツィーです
responses.english: It's sweet and a little fruity
responses.listen_for: 甘い = sweet, 少し = a little, フルーツィー = fruity. Combine these words to understand the profile.

responses.japanese: 辛口でスモーキーな味わいです
responses.romaji: Karakuchi de sumoookii na ajiwai desu
responses.english: It has a dry, smoky flavor
responses.listen_for: 辛口 (karakuchi) = dry. スモーキー = smoky. 味わい (ajiwai) = flavor/taste profile.

responses.japanese: 柑橘系の香りとハーブのような後味があります
responses.romaji: Kankitsu-kei no kaori to haabu no you na ato-aji ga arimasu
responses.english: It has a citrus aroma with an herbal finish
responses.listen_for: 柑橘 (kankitsu) = citrus. 香り (kaori) = aroma. 後味 (atoaji) = finish/aftertaste. You're getting a real cocktail description.

phrases.japanese: もう一杯お願いします
phrases.notes: 一杯 = one glass/drink.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.listen_for: Order received. Same again is coming.

responses.japanese: 同じものでよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Onaji mono de yoroshii desu ka?
responses.listen_for: 同じ (onaji) = same. They're confirming you want a repeat. Say はい or point to something new on the menu.

phrases.japanese: 甘くないものが好きです
phrases.romaji: Amaku nai mono ga suki desu
phrases.notes: Great for directing the bartender.

responses.japanese: では、〜はいかがですか？
responses.listen_for: では (dewa) = then/in that case. いかが = how about? They're tailoring a recommendation. Say お願いします.

phrases.japanese: これは何のベーススピリッツですか？
phrases.romaji: Kore wa nani no beesu supirittsu desu ka?
phrases.english: What is the base spirit in this?
phrases.notes: Shows genuine cocktail knowledge.

responses.japanese: ベースは〜を使っています
responses.listen_for: 使っています (tsukatte imasu) = is using. They'll name the spirit. You might also hear 自家製 (jikasei) = house-made.

phrases.japanese: 日本のウイスキーを試してみたいです
phrases.romaji: Nihon no uisukii wo tameshite mitai desu
phrases.english: I'd like to try a Japanese whisky
phrases.notes: Opens the door to Nikka, Suntory, craft expressions.

responses.japanese: シングルモルトとブレンデッド、どちらがよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Shinguru moruto to burendeddo, dochira ga yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: Would you prefer single malt or blended?
responses.listen_for: シングルモルト = single malt. ブレンデッド = blended. A real whisky conversation just started.

responses.japanese: ニッカとサントリー、どちらの方が好きですか？
responses.romaji: Nikka to Santori, dochira no hou ga suki desu ka?
responses.english: Do you prefer Nikka or Suntory?
responses.listen_for: The two big houses. If you don't know yet, say まだ分かりません (I don't know yet).

phrases.japanese: ハイボールをお願いします
phrases.notes: Japan's most popular bar drink. Ridiculously well-made.

responses.japanese: ウイスキーは何になさいますか？
responses.romaji: Uisukii wa nani ni nasaimasu ka?
responses.listen_for: 何になさいますか = what will you have? They're asking which whisky for your highball.

responses.japanese: 濃さはいかがしますか？
responses.english: How strong would you like it?
responses.listen_for: 濃さ (kosa) = strength/concentration. 濃いめ (koime) = stronger, 薄め (usume) = weaker, 普通 (futsuu) = standard.

phrases.japanese: 乾杯！
phrases.notes: Make eye contact with each person as you clink.

responses.japanese: 乾杯！
responses.listen_for: They'll echo it back. Make eye contact — not doing so is considered rude.

phrases.japanese: ノンアルコールのカクテルはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Non-arukooru no kakuteru wa arimasu ka?
phrases.notes: Mocktail culture is growing in Japan.

responses.japanese: はい、モクテルをご用意しております
responses.romaji: Hai, mokuteru wo go-youi shite orimasu
responses.listen_for: モクテル = mocktail. ご用意 (go-youi) = prepared/available.

responses.japanese: 申し訳ありませんが、アルコールのみです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, arukooru nomi desu
responses.listen_for: のみ = only. Not every bar does mocktails yet, especially traditional ones.

phrases.japanese: バーテンダーさんはどれくらいこのバーで働いていますか？
phrases.romaji: Baatendaa-san wa dorekurai kono baa de hataraite imasu ka?
phrases.english: How long have you been working at this bar?
phrases.notes: Great conversation starter. Japanese bartenders train for years.

responses.japanese: 〜年になります
responses.listen_for: 年 (nen) = years. A bartender saying 10年 (juunen/10 years) or more is not unusual.

responses.japanese: 修行は〜年しました
responses.listen_for: 修行 (shugyou) = training/apprenticeship. This is the craft tradition — they apprenticed under a master.

phrases.japanese: このカクテルの作り方を教えてもらえますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono kakuteru no tsukurikata wo oshiete moraemasu ka?
phrases.english: Could you tell me how this cocktail is made?
phrases.notes: Japanese bartenders will give you a thorough, proud answer.

responses.japanese: まず〜を使って、次に〜を加えます
responses.romaji: Mazu [ingredient] wo tsukatte, tsugi ni [ingredient] wo kuwaemasu
responses.english: First I use [ingredient], then I add [ingredient]
responses.listen_for: まず (mazu) = first. 次に (tsugi ni) = next. 加えます (kuwaemasu) = add.

phrases.japanese: 今夜のスペシャルは何ですか？
phrases.romaji: Konya no supesharu wa nan desu ka?
phrases.notes: Seasonal and nightly specials are common.

responses.japanese: 今夜は〜を使った季節のカクテルです
responses.romaji: Konya wa [ingredient] wo tsukatta kisetsu no kakuteru desu
responses.english: Tonight it's a seasonal cocktail using [ingredient]
responses.listen_for: 季節 (kisetsu) = seasonal. 救った/使った (tsukatta) = using. This is the bartender's creative pick.

phrases.japanese: お水も一緒にいただけますか？
phrases.romaji: Omizu mo issho ni itadakemasu ka?
phrases.english: Could I also have some water?
phrases.notes: Stay hydrated — Japanese cocktails are deceptively smooth.

responses.japanese: はい、もちろんです
responses.listen_for: もちろんです = of course. Completely normal to ask.

phrases.japanese: 〜に行きたいんですが
phrases.notes: The んですが softens it into a request.

responses.japanese: ここから歩いて〜分ぐらいです
responses.romaji: Koko kara aruite [X] fun gurai desu
responses.english: It's about [X] minutes walk from here
responses.listen_for: 歩いて (aruite) = walking. 分 = minutes. ぐらい = about/approximately.

responses.japanese: 電車で行った方がいいですよ
responses.romaji: Densha de itta hou ga ii desu yo
responses.english: It's better to go by train
responses.listen_for: 電車 (densha) = train. 方がいい = better to. They're steering you to public transport.

phrases.japanese: まっすぐ行ってください
phrases.notes: Key direction words: まっすぐ/右/左.

responses.japanese: 〜メートル先に〜があります
responses.listen_for: メートル = meters. 先 (saki) = ahead. They're giving you a landmark to aim for.

phrases.japanese: ここから遠いですか？
phrases.notes: 近いです (chikai desu) = it is close.

responses.japanese: いいえ、近いですよ。歩いて〜分です
responses.romaji: Iie, chikai desu yo. Aruite [X] fun desu
responses.english: No, it's close. [X] minutes on foot
responses.listen_for: 近い (chikai) = close/nearby. 歩いて = walking. The number before 分 is your walk time.

responses.japanese: 少し遠いです。バスか電車がいいですよ
responses.romaji: Sukoshi tooi desu. Basu ka densha ga ii desu yo
responses.english: It's a bit far. Bus or train would be better
responses.listen_for: 少し遠い (sukoshi tooi) = a bit far. か = or. They're recommending transport.

phrases.japanese: 地図を描いてもらえますか？
phrases.english: Could you draw me a map?
phrases.notes: Japanese people are incredibly helpful — many will walk you there.

responses.japanese: はい、ちょっと待ってください
responses.listen_for: ちょっと待ってください = wait a moment. They're grabbing a pen or phone.

responses.japanese: 一緒に行きましょうか？
responses.listen_for: 一緒に (issho ni) = together. 行きましょうか = shall we go? They're offering to escort you. Say ありがとうございます!

phrases.japanese: トイレはどこですか？
phrases.notes: Japanese public toilets are world-class.

responses.japanese: あちらです
responses.listen_for: あちら = over there. They'll point. Follow the direction.

responses.japanese: 〜階にございます
responses.listen_for: 階 (kai) = floor. In department stores toilets are often on a specific floor.

phrases.japanese: 助けてください！
phrases.notes: Loud and clear. People will respond.

responses.japanese: どうしましたか？
responses.listen_for: どうしましたか = what's wrong / what happened? Be ready to point or show a translation.

phrases.japanese: 救急車を呼んでください
phrases.notes: Emergency numbers: 119 (ambulance/fire), 110 (police).

responses.japanese: すぐに呼びます
responses.listen_for: すぐ = immediately. Help is being called.

phrases.japanese: パスポートをなくしました
phrases.notes: Go to the nearest 交番 (koban / police box) first.

responses.japanese: 交番に行ってください
responses.english: Please go to the police box
responses.listen_for: 交番 (kouban) = small police box/koban. These are everywhere in Japan and very helpful.

responses.japanese: いつ、どこでなくしましたか？
responses.english: When and where did you lose it?
responses.listen_for: いつ = when. どこ = where. Answer as best you can.

phrases.japanese: 具合が悪いです
phrases.notes: 痛い (itai) = it hurts. Point at where.

responses.japanese: どこが痛いですか？
responses.listen_for: どこ = where. 痛い = hurt/pain. Point at the affected area.

responses.japanese: 病院に行った方がいいです
responses.romaji: Byouin ni itta hou ga ii desu
responses.english: You should go to a hospital
responses.listen_for: 病院 (byouin) = hospital. 方がいい = should/better to.

phrases.japanese: 大使館に電話してください
phrases.notes: Know your country's embassy number before you go.

responses.japanese: 分かりました。どこの国ですか？
responses.romaji: Wakarimashita. Doko no kuni desu ka?
responses.listen_for: どこの国 (doko no kuni) = which country. State your country clearly.

phrases.japanese: 一、二、三、四、五、六、七、八、九、十
phrases.romaji: Ichi, ni, san, shi, go, roku, nana, hachi, kyuu, juu

responses.japanese: 〜円です
responses.listen_for: Numbers you need most: 百 (100), 千 (1000), 万 (10,000). Most prices fall between 500–5000.

phrases.japanese: 何時ですか？
phrases.notes: 時 (ji) = o'clock, 分 (fun) = minutes.

responses.japanese: 〜時〜分です
responses.listen_for: Listen for the number before 時 (hour) and before 分 (minutes). E.g., 3時半 (sanji han) = 3:30.

phrases.japanese: 〜時に予約があります
phrases.notes: Useful when arriving at a restaurant or hotel.

responses.japanese: お名前をお願いします
responses.listen_for: お名前 (onamae) = name. Say your name clearly or show it written.

phrases.japanese: 〜から来ました
phrases.notes: Standard reply when asked where you are from.

responses.japanese: 〜からですか！遠いですね！
responses.romaji: [country] kara desu ka! Tooi desu ne!
responses.listen_for: 遠い (tooi) = far. Japanese locals appreciate knowing where visitors are visiting from.

phrases.japanese: 日本は初めてです
phrases.english: This is my first time in Japan
phrases.notes: If it's your second time, say: 2回目です (Nikaime desu).

responses.japanese: ようこそ日本へ！楽しんでくださいね
responses.romaji: Youkoso Nihon e! Tanoshinde kudasai ne
responses.english: Welcome to Japan! Please enjoy your stay
responses.listen_for: ようこそ (youkoso) = welcome. 楽しんで (tanoshinde) = enjoy.

phrases.japanese: 日本のご飯はとても美味しいです
phrases.romaji: Nihon no gohan wa totemo oishii desu
phrases.notes: Guaranteed warm smile from locals.

responses.japanese: 本当ですか？何が一番好きですか？
responses.romaji: Hontou desu ka? Nani ga ichiban suki desu ka?
responses.english: Really? What do you like the most?
responses.listen_for: 一番好き (ichiban suki) = favorite/like the most. Name a dish like ラーメン or 寿司!

phrases.japanese: 今日は寒いですね
phrases.notes: Great winter icebreaker in December.

responses.japanese: そうですね、風邪を引かないようにしてくださいね
responses.romaji: Sou desu ne, kaze wo hikanai you ni shite kudasai ne
responses.english: Indeed, make sure you stay warm and don't catch a cold
responses.listen_for: そうですね = 'I agree / indeed'. A universal casual agreement phrase.

phrases.japanese: 写真を撮ってもらえますか？
phrases.english: Could you take a photo for me?
phrases.notes: Hand over your phone or camera after asking.

responses.japanese: はい、いいですよ！はい、チーズ！
responses.romaji: Hai, ii desu yo! Hai, chiizu!
responses.listen_for: チーズ (chiizu) = cheese! Smile for the shutter.

phrases.japanese: ここで写真を撮ってもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Koko de shashin wo totte mo ii desu ka?
phrases.english: May I take a photo here?
phrases.notes: Crucial at temples, shrines, or private collections.

responses.japanese: すみません、撮影禁止です
responses.listen_for: 撮影禁止 (satsuei kinshi) = no photography allowed.

phrases.japanese: タトゥーは大丈夫ですか？
phrases.notes: Check policies beforehand if you have visible ink.

responses.japanese: シールで隠せば大丈夫です
responses.english: It's fine if you cover them with a sticker
responses.listen_for: 隠せば (kakuseba) = if covered. They may offer cover-up patches.

responses.japanese: 申し訳ありませんが、お断りしております
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, okotowari shite orimasu
responses.english: I'm sorry, but tattoos are not permitted
responses.listen_for: お断り (okotowari) = refusal / not permitted.

phrases.japanese: 露天風呂はどこですか？
phrases.notes: 露天風呂 (rotenburo) = outdoor open-air bath.

responses.japanese: 奥の階段を下りたところにございます
responses.romaji: Oku no kaidan wo orita tokoro ni gozaimasu
responses.english: It is located down the stairs at the back
responses.listen_for: 奥 (oku) = back/inner part, 階段 (kaidan) = stairs.
